judgements.reason: Integral lattices is already complete in Tau Ceti: discriminant groups, the Nikulin overlattice correspondence and the isometry D₈⁺ ≅ E₈ are all built. Analytic toric geometry still needs Gordan's lemma, affine toric schemes and fan gluing, complex-manifold charts and gluing, the orbit–cone and boundary theory, the properness criterion and the algebraic–analytic comparison.

Dense graph limits already has counting, weak regularity, the cut-distance triangle inequality, total boundedness and sampling concentration; about four stacked layers remain (Lovász–Szegedy compactness, inverse counting, representability, the Diaconis–Janson mixture theorem). Toric geometry has only cones, fans and mixed-monomial charts, and about six stacked layers remain (affine toric schemes and fan gluing, manifold charts and gluing, orbit–cone correspondence with SNC boundary, toric maps and properness, the scheme comparison), which is slightly more theory.

Classical groups has scaffolding (standard and tensor-power representations, Weyl modules, weight spaces, Schur–Weyl, the combinatorial Weyl dimension and GT counts) but no representation theorems. The group-level highest-weight classification for GLₙ, SLₙ, SOₙ, Spₙ and Oₙ, characters as Schur polynomials, branching rules and Gelfand–Tsetlin bases with Capelli-type generators are all missing, which is far more than dense graph limits still lacks: compactness, inverse counting, representability and mixture/sampling theorems over a built graphon core.

Classical groups lacks the group-level highest-weight classification, character and dimension formulas, branching and Gelfand–Tsetlin bases. Modular forms, beyond its large Hecke/newform base, still needs Eisenstein series with character, bad-prime newform and L-function theory, modular symbols with coefficient fields, the LMFDB layer and the Eichler–Selberg trace formula. Its dimension formulas also need unbuilt Fuchsian compact Riemann surfaces plus analytic Riemann–Roch and Serre duality, a much larger and deeper stack.

Shimura data needs Weil restriction and the Deligne torus, real Lie groups with Cartan involutions and Hermitian symmetric domains, homogeneous VHS, compact duals with reflex-field descent, adelic points and van Est, on top of Tau Ceti's large algebraic-group and Hodge libraries. Modular forms needs slightly more in total: the newform, bad-prime and L-function completions, modular symbols and coefficient fields, the LMFDB layer and trace formula, and for the dimension formulas a further tower of Fuchsian compact Riemann surfaces, Riemann–Hurwitz and Forster's analytic Riemann–Roch.

Shimura data builds on Tau Ceti's extensive reductive-group, parabolic and Hodge-structure libraries, and still needs Weil restriction, Cartan involutions with Hermitian symmetric domains, VHS and compact duals with reflex-field descent. The Jacobian has only divisors, line bundles and Ext-defined cohomology, and must build coherent cohomology with Serre duality, cohomology and base change, symmetric powers, fppf Picard-functor representability, and the cube theorem, dual abelian variety and polarizations: slightly more foundational theory.

The Jacobian challenge needs coherent and relative cohomology, Picard representability and abelian-variety duality. Automorphic bundles needs that theory generalized to abelian schemes (duals, Picard functors, Dieudonné deformation), plus Shimura data, canonical models of Shimura varieties, Baily–Borel and toroidal compactifications, PEL moduli, resolution of singularities and GAGA, all before its own canonical extensions (prerequisite depth 28 stages).

Classical adic étale cohomology needs about 80 external stages (depth 19): scheme étale cohomology with Verdier and Poincaré duality (also importing the Jacobian), nearby cycles, perfectoid spaces and quotients, adic étale geometry, enhanced derived sheaves, then Huber's comparison theorems. Automorphic bundles needs about 93 (depth 28): Shimura data, canonical models, Baily–Borel and toroidal compactifications with degenerations of abelian schemes, PEL and Hilbert moduli, resolution of singularities and GAGA, so it is slightly larger and deeper.

Stable reduction needs the Jacobian's Picard and abelian-variety contracts plus nodal curves, dualizing sheaves, relative Proj and descent, arithmetic-surface intersection theory, resolution, minimal models and stabilization. Classical adic étale cohomology also imports the Jacobian (through étale trace and purity), and adds scheme étale cohomology with Verdier duality, perfectoid spaces and quotients, ∞-categorical derived sheaves, adic étale geometry and all of Huber's theory.

Stable reduction needs the Jacobian's Picard and abelian-variety theory plus arithmetic surfaces (blowups, intersection theory, resolution, minimal models), Artin–Winters semistable reduction, Knudsen stabilization and stable maps. Heegaard Floer, beyond its built Fredholm, Sard–Smale and Morse-lemma base, needs somewhat more: Morse homology, the Cauchy–Riemann elliptic package with Maslov index, Gromov compactness, transversality and gluing, Lagrangian Floer homology, HF-hat invariance in Sym^g(Σ), staged HF± and naturality, and reconciliations such as lattice = HF⁻ and grid = HFK.

Heegaard Floer's missing tower is analytic and topological: elliptic Cauchy–Riemann theory, compactness and gluing, Floer homology and invariance in Sym^g. Automorphic congruences sits on about 590 unbuilt prerequisite stages before the Skinner–Urban and Fouquet–Wan arguments: GL₂ Galois representations and modularity lifting, unitary Shimura varieties with compactifications and Hida families, Kato and Heegner Euler systems, Gross–Zagier heights, p-adic L-functions, p-adic local Langlands and completed cohomology.

AGR-II's GLₙ constructions need about 320 closure stages: Shimura varieties with compactifications and automorphic bundles, étale and adic cohomology with weights, endoscopic transfer and local Langlands, eigenvarieties. The automorphic-congruences closure contains 302 of those and adds about 295 more (Kato, Heegner and Beilinson–Flach Euler systems, Gross–Zagier, Serre's conjecture and GL₂ modularity lifting, p-adic L-functions, (φ,Γ)-modules, K-theory) before its own U(2,2) and U(3,1) congruence arguments.

PAI imports AGR-II's final export AG2.7, and with it 319 of the 320 stages of AGR-II's closure. On top of that it needs Caraiani–Scholze torsion concentration (Igusa varieties, perfectoid Shimura varieties, Hodge–Tate period maps), torsion and completed cohomology, Galois deformation rings with derived patching, and its own degree-shifting and ultrapatching layers.

Prismatic cohomology needs about 100 closure stages: ∞-categorical derived sheaves, derived de Rham and crystalline theory, perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves, A_inf cohomology and THH trace methods. PAI's closure contains 80 of those and about 300 more, namely all of AGR-II, Shimura varieties and compactifications, étale cohomology with weights, endoscopic transfer, Igusa varieties, deformation rings and patching.

Integral lattices is fully built in Tau Ceti, including the overlattice correspondence and D₈⁺ ≅ E₈. Dense graph limits still lacks Lovász–Szegedy compactness, the inverse counting lemma and convergence equivalence, representability of graph parameters, the Diaconis–Janson mixture theorem and sampling convergence.

Prismatic cohomology needs about 100 closure stages of derived and ∞-categorical algebra, crystalline and derived de Rham theory, perfectoid spaces and diamonds, A_inf cohomology and THH. AGR-II's closure includes 80 of these and about 240 more, namely Shimura varieties and compactifications, automorphic bundles, étale cohomology with weights and duality, endoscopic transfer with local Langlands, and eigenvarieties, before its own GLₙ constructions.

The Jacobian needs coherent and relative cohomology, Picard representability and abelian-variety theory. Classical adic étale cohomology imports the Jacobian through its étale trace/purity stage, and further needs scheme étale cohomology with Verdier duality, nearby cycles, perfectoid spaces, adic étale geometry, enhanced derived sheaves and Huber's comparison theorems.

PAI needs AGR-II, Caraiani–Scholze torsion concentration, completed and torsion cohomology and patching: about 380 closure stages. The automorphic-congruences closure shares about 320 of those and adds about 280 more, including Kato, Heegner and Beilinson–Flach Euler systems, Gross–Zagier, Serre's conjecture and GL₂ modularity lifting, Hilbert and metaplectic forms, p-adic L-functions, K-theory and (φ,Γ)-modules.

Heegaard Floer needs a large analytic and topological tower (Morse homology, Cauchy–Riemann elliptic theory, Gromov compactness and gluing, Floer homology, HF-hat in Sym^g, reconciliations), but it starts from Tau Ceti's Fredholm, Sard–Smale, Sobolev and J-holomorphic foundations. Prismatic cohomology has no δ-rings or crystalline theory to start from and needs about 95 unbuilt prerequisite stages before its own nine layers: ∞-categorical derived sheaves and animated rings, derived de Rham and de Rham–Witt theory, perfectoid spaces, diamonds and Fargues–Fontaine curves, A_inf cohomology, THH and cyclotomic spectra.

Toric geometry needs affine toric schemes and gluing, complex-manifold charts and gluing, orbit and boundary theory, properness and a toric comparison; all are fairly elementary constructions on existing cone and fan code. Shimura data needs Weil restriction and the Deligne torus, real Lie groups with Cartan involutions and Hermitian symmetric domains, VHS, flag-variety compact duals with reflex-field descent, adelic points and van Est.

Stable reduction needs the Jacobian contracts plus arithmetic surfaces, semistable reduction, stabilization and stable maps. Automorphic bundles needs abelian schemes with duals and deformation theory, Hilbert/Quot schemes, algebraic stacks and resolution of singularities, together with Shimura data, canonical models, Baily–Borel and toroidal compactifications, PEL moduli, GAGA and p-adic Hodge prefixes, all before its canonical extensions.

Integral lattices is complete in Tau Ceti. Classical groups still lacks the highest-weight classification of irreducible representations of GLₙ, SLₙ, SOₙ, Spₙ and Oₙ, characters as Schur polynomials, the dimension and branching theorems, and Gelfand–Tsetlin bases and generators.

Dense graph limits lacks compactness, inverse counting, representability and the mixture and sampling theorems, over an already built graphon core. Modular forms lacks Eisenstein series with character, bad-prime newform and L-function theory, modular symbols and coefficient fields, Galois/LMFDB invariants and the trace formula, plus Fuchsian compact Riemann surfaces with analytic Riemann–Roch for the dimension formulas.

Stable reduction's missing theory is the algebraic geometry of curves: the Jacobian contracts, arithmetic surfaces and minimal models, semistable reduction, stabilization and stable maps. Automorphic congruences needs about 590 unbuilt stages, among them Néron models and semistable abelian varieties, Shimura varieties with compactifications, Galois deformation and modularity lifting, Euler systems, p-adic L-functions and p-adic Hodge theory.

The Jacobian challenge needs coherent and relative cohomology, Picard-functor representability, abelian-variety duality and the Abel–Jacobi universal property. Heegaard Floer needs a much larger tower: Morse homology, the Cauchy–Riemann elliptic package with Maslov index, Gromov compactness, transversality and gluing, Lagrangian Floer homology, HF-hat invariance in Sym^g(Σ), staged HF± and naturality, and reconciliations with grid and lattice homology.
